newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Pound strength dampens BOC profit rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Pound strength dampens BOC profit rise.

text.p: First-quarter profits at BOC Group Plc rose two percent but the health and industrial gases giant said on Thursday the increase was hampered by persistent strength of the pound.

Pre-tax profit rose to 102.7 million pounds ($166.1 million) from 100.8 million a year earlier, right in the middle of market expectations. The result would have been five million pounds, or seven percent, higher if the currency impact was excluded.
"Things are going pretty well, although the currency is taking a little bit of the shine off it," chief executive Danny Rosenkranz told Reuters.
Shares in BOC eased 1-1/2 pence to 936-1/2 pence in late morning trading on the London Stock Exchange.
Industrial gases, which are used in industries as varied as foods, chemicals, metallurgy and water purification, saw operating profits rise to 96.4 million pounds from 94.1 million.
The sector's results were particularly good in Japan, while profits also rose in Europe, the south Pacific and Asia.
Profits in the vacuum business, however, fell 13 percent to 12.1 million pounds following the collapse in the vacuum pump order book in the second half of 1996.

The fall was well flagged and widely expected by industry analysts. BOC said the vacuum business, which specialises in machinery for super-cleaning semiconductor factories, was in good shape and seemed to have had the worst behind it.
Order intake had begun to pick up, although it was still only 50 to 60 percent of the levels seen a year ago.
"If we move on into the next year, we should be on the way up and the year after that we should be flying," Rosenkrantz said.
BOC's health care business saw operating profit retreat to 13.0 million pounds from 13.5 million but the results would have been unchanged if currency effects were ignored.

The business continued to suffer from lower prices for anaesthetic gas Forane but this was offset by higher sales of the Suprane anaesthetic. Rosenkrantz repeated that the sector's results for the year as a whole would be flat before recovering the following 12 months.
"The currency made that assumption a little bit tighter but that is still what we're trying to do," he said.
